items.title: The big August jobs report is due out Friday. Here's what to expect for what has been a jobless summer
items.body: August nonfarm payrolls are expected to rise by 53,000 as a subdued labor market keeps Fed attention focused on inflation.

items.title: Fed Governor Waller indicates he will support holding rates steady at September meeting
items.body: In remarks that seem to contrast with statements last week from Chairman Kevin Warsh, Waller expressed confidence in the current inflation trends.

items.title: 'Danger zone of extreme weather': UN warns of supersized El Niño set to hit global economy and markets
items.body: Latest modeling shows high risks of floods, drought and extreme heat persisting until February 2027.

items.title: South Korea's semiconductor exports just tripled year-over-year. Is it too much of a good thing?
items.body: If growth were to slow in the semiconductor sector, would the slowdown take the Korean economy with it?

items.title: Private payrolls rose by 38,000 in August, less than expected, ADP reports
items.body: Though job creation held positive, August was the smallest gain since January and reflective of a broader slowdown in the labor market.

items.title: Euro zone inflation is back above 3%. Higher interest rates are likely to follow
items.body: The European Central Bank is seen hiking rates in September as the Iran war raises energy costs in the region.

items.title: Bank of England chief warns new AI models threaten global financial stability
items.body: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey has warned that frontier AI could materially increase cyber risks to the global financial system.

items.title: India’s economy expands 7.8% in fiscal first quarter, beating estimates
items.body: The economy was driven by a strong performance in the financial, real estate, information technology and professional services sectors.
